title: Fitness platform
description: Workout Tracking, Training Progress and Billing (OpenTelemetry via Alloy), RabbitMQ and Valkey (scraped by Alloy), traces in Tempo, logs in Loki, and the alert rules. Provisioned from infrastructure/grafana/dashboards/.

list.name: version
list.label: Version
list.description: service.version: the build (git describe) or the version a deployment names. During a rolling deploy, the old and the new version side by side; the HTTP panels split by it.

list.name: interface
list.label: Interface
list.description: How the interactions reached the platform: graphql, telegram (the bot), rest, or rabbitmq (a message no interaction started). Filters the traces and logs panels; metrics don't carry it.

options.content:
**A trace** is one roundtrip and what it causes, across both services: a recording runs from Workout Tracking's `POST .../recordings` to Training Progress' policies. Open one from the *Traces* panels, or from a log (its `trace_id`).

**A flow** is a member's interaction over several roundtrips (`baggage: session.id=<flow id>`): type its id in the **flow** box above to see its traces and logs.

Dashboards and alert rules are files in `infrastructure/grafana/`.

panels.title: Service: $service (one row per service: workout-tracking, training-progress, billing)
Requests per minute, by version
panels.description: This service's HTTP requests (GraphQL is POST /graphql).

panels.title: Client and server errors per minute
panels.description: 4xx (rejected input, 404, 409, 429) and 5xx, by status.

panels.title: Request duration p95 and p99
panels.description: The alert fires on p95 over 1 s (ADR 1).

panels.title: Database operation duration p95 and p99
panels.description: Its own PostgreSQL: each service has one.

panels.title: Stripe events per minute, by type and outcome
panels.description: billing_stripe_events_total: applied, ignored (not a membership's), duplicate (a resend, applied once), failed (Stripe sends it again; alert).

panels.title: Webhooks refused by their signature check
panels.description: webhooks_verification_failures_total, by receiver and reason: a wrong signing secret, or someone posting to the route (alert).

panels.title: Billing's integration events published per minute, by topic
panels.description: membership-started.v1 and membership-ended.v1 to RabbitMQ, from Tempo's span metrics (the relay's spans); Training Progress' goal allowances follow them.

panels.title: Stripe API calls p95 and p99
panels.description: Checkouts and the billing portal call Stripe; the outgoing-calls alert fires on p95 over 5 s.

panels.title: Requests per minute, by service and version
Requests per minute, by endpoint
panels.description: The 20-per-minute alert watches each of these lines.

panels.title: Server errors (5xx) per minute, by endpoint and version

targets.expr: sum by (service_name, service_version, http_route) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{deployment_environment_name=~"$env", service_name=~"$service", service_version=~"$version", http_response_status_code=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval])) * 60

panels.title: Request duration p95, by service and version

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (service_name, service_version, le) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{deployment_environment_name=~"$env", service_name=~"$service", service_version=~"$version"}[$__rate_interval])))

topk(10, sum by (service_name, http_request_method, http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{deployment_environment_name=~"$env", service_name=~"$service", service_version=~"$version"}[1h])))

panels.title: Operations per minute, by type and root fields
panels.description: graphql_server_operation_duration_seconds: every GraphQL request is POST /graphql to the HTTP metric. The 20-per-minute alert watches each line.

panels.title: Failed operations per minute, by error code
Operation duration p95, by root fields
Request duration p95 and p99, by service
panels.description: Incoming HTTP requests. p99 shows the slowest 1%, where timeouts start.

panels.title: GraphQL operation duration p95 and p99, by root fields
panels.description: Training Progress' GraphQL operations.

panels.title: Database operation duration p95 and p99, by operation
panels.description: PostgreSQL statements, by operation (SELECT, INSERT...). Rises before the HTTP percentiles when the database is the cause.

panels.title: Outgoing HTTP calls p95 and p99, by host
panels.description: Calls the services make: Telegram, mail and any other API.

panels.title: Message handling p95 and p99, the 10 slowest spans
panels.description: Tempo's span metrics for consumer and internal spans: message handlers, policies, the outbox. Work no HTTP request measures. The 10 slowest at each percentile.

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (service, span_name, le) (rate(traces_spanmetrics_latency_bucket{service=~"$service", span_kind=~"SPAN_KIND_CONSUMER|SPAN_KIND_INTERNAL"}[$__rate_interval]))))

topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (service, span_name, le) (rate(traces_spanmetrics_latency_bucket{service=~"$service", span_kind=~"SPAN_KIND_CONSUMER|SPAN_KIND_INTERNAL"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Calls between services p99 (service graph)
panels.description: From Tempo's service graph: the server side of each call, client → server.

panels.title: Valkey command latency p99, by command
panels.description: Valkey's own latency per command, from INFO (microseconds).

panels.title: Garbage collection pauses p99
panels.description: V8's GC pauses, which stop the process.

panels.title: Rate limit, timeouts and faults (section 16; faults are the orange annotations)
Rate-limited requests per minute, by handler
panels.description: Requests rejected past RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE from one caller: 429, with TOO_MANY_REQUESTS over GraphQL (rate_limit_rejected_requests_total).

panels.title: Timeouts per minute, by entrypoint
panels.description: Queries that took longer than QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS: 504 over HTTP, TIMEOUT over GraphQL. Their work goes on in the background, holding a database connection (resilience_events_total).

panels.title: Rejected and failed responses per minute
panels.description: What callers saw: HTTP 429 (GraphQL's TOO_MANY_REQUESTS too, on /graphql) and 5xx (504 is a timeout) by route, and GraphQL operations that failed with TIMEOUT or INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, which answer 200.

targets.expr: sum by (service_name, http_route, http_response_status_code) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{http_response_status_code=~"429|5..", deployment_environment_name=~"$env", service_name=~"$service", service_version=~"$version"}[$__rate_interval])) * 60

panels.title: Requests waiting for a database connection
panels.description: Callers queued for one of the pool's 25 connections: the database is slow, or timed-out queries still hold connections (db_client_connection_pending_requests).

panels.title: Read cache and load tests (sections 8.2 and 17; load tests are the purple annotations)
Read cache: reads per minute, by read model and result
panels.description: How the cached read models were answered (read_cache_reads_total): hit (from Valkey), load (from PostgreSQL, after a miss), wait (another caller's load, under the load lock), off (READ_CACHE=off), unavailable (Valkey down).

panels.title: Loads from PostgreSQL per minute, by read model
panels.description: The reads the cache didn't answer. A cache stampede is a spike here: many loads of the same keys at once, with READ_CACHE_LOCK=off. With the load lock, one load per key and miss.

panels.title: Database operations per second, by service and version
panels.description: What the read models and the writes cost PostgreSQL (db_client_operation_duration_seconds_count).

panels.title: Recent traces
panels.description: The latest traces of the services, in the interface picked above (with All, every trace).

panels.title: Flow: the roundtrips of one interaction (type its id in the flow box)
Database operation duration p95, by service
RabbitMQ (built-in Prometheus metrics, scraped by Alloy)
Messages per queue (ready and unacknowledged)
panels.description: The not-consumed and over-5-messages alerts watch these.

panels.title: Evicted and expired keys per second
Errors and warnings: the services, RabbitMQ and Valkey
panels.description: Errors and warnings in the interface picked above. RabbitMQ's and Valkey's own logs have no interface: they show with All only.
